info.title: ETL Console customer API
info.summary: Start work, follow it, decide on it, and be told when something happens.
info.description:
The public contract for an organisation's own portals and systems. Generic: any pipeline, any form,
any event type. The console is the organisation's admin tool; this API is how their systems reach the platform.

- Auth: OAuth 2.0 client credentials (POST /v1/oauth/token), per-organisation API clients with scopes.
- Errors: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json).
- Lists: cursor paging (limit, cursor -> nextCursor).
- Creating POSTs take an Idempotency-Key header.
- Times: RFC 3339 in UTC.
- Rate limits per client and per workspace: RateLimit-* headers on every answer, 429 with Retry-After
  (`/problems/rate-limited`). A workspace may have a monthly quota of calls: Quota-* headers, a Quota-Warning from 80%,
  and past it 429 `/problems/quota-exceeded` until the month ends -- the bill's month, a calendar month in the
  workspace's billing time zone (America/Chicago unless set).
- Every call that passes the checks is billed as `api.calls` (per 1,000, on the workspace's rate card); the token
  endpoint and signed links are not. Webhook deliveries that arrive are billed as `webhook.deliveries`.
- Embeddable run view: POST /v1/runs/{runId}/view-links answers a 15-minute link to a read-only page of the run that a
  portal may frame from the origins its API client allows.

post.summary: Exchange the client's id and secret for an access token (15 minutes).

scope.description: Space-separated; a subset of the client's scopes. Omit for all.

get.summary: The pipelines this client may start or read.
One pipeline, with its input contract and the event types its runs emit.

post.summary: Start a run with a record and/or uploaded files (push intake).
post.description: The record is validated against the pipeline's input contract first; nothing is stored when it fails (422, each field's path under "record"). Every file id must be one of the workspace's own files (422 at "files[i]"). The record and the files are handed to the run as its intake: one JSON object with the record's fields and the start's own under names beginning with "_" (_reference, _files, _file_ids, _file_bucket, _file_key, ...). One run of a pipeline is in flight at a time (409 while one is). Sending the same Idempotency-Key again returns the first run. `parameters` are the run's parameter values by name, checked as the pipeline declares them (GET /pipelines/{id} lists them): a name it does not declare, a value of the wrong type or a required one with no value and no default is a 422 at "parameters.<name>", and nothing starts. Run and wait: with `wait` (1 to 60 seconds), the answer waits for the run to end -- ended in time, 200 with the run and its `result` (a completed run's final output, as GET /runs/{runId}/result gives it); still going, the 202 and its Location, as without `wait`. A replay with the same Idempotency-Key waits again for the same run. With `wait`, `format` (or the Accept header) chooses the waited answer's format, as GET /runs/{runId}/result's: json (the default, the Run and its result); pdf, html or md -- once the run ends, exactly what GET /runs/{runId}/result answers in that format (the document, or its problem: a run that did not complete is a 409 run-not-completed), always with the run's Location. An unsupported format is a 400 and nothing starts.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to wait for the run to end, 1 to 60 (`30` or `30s`). Absent: answer at once (202).

200.description: Run and wait: the run ended within `wait` -- the run, and its result when it completed (json); or, with `format` pdf, html or md, the run's result as that document.

text/markdown.example:
From signed report RPT-0093 version 1

> Made from the report's HTML. Markdown is never signed: the PDF is the record.

# Patient intake summary

post.summary: Run a pipeline once for each day (hour, week) of a past range, a few at a time.
post.description: Makes a backfill: one run of the pipeline for each period of `from`..`to` (both days included), counted in the workspace's billing time zone (America/Chicago unless set) -- a day is midnight to midnight there, so 23 or 25 hours on a daylight-saving day; an hour is a clock hour; a week is seven days from each start day. Each run's steps read `{{run.date}}` (the period's day), `{{run.windowStart}}` and `{{run.windowEnd}}` (its bounds, RFC 3339 with the zone's offset) and every `{{param.name}}` of `parameters`. At most 366 periods, and nothing that has not begun yet. A period that already has a completed run of the pipeline (a scheduled run whose slot falls in it, or an earlier backfill's) is skipped unless `rerunCompleted` is true. Answered once the backfill is made; its runs are queued gradually, at most `concurrency` at a time (1 to 4, as the platform's memory budget allows), beside the pipeline's own runs, and each is billed as any run. Refused (409, the problem's `type` says why) when the workspace already has 3 open backfills (`too-many-backfills`), a period is in another open backfill of the pipeline (`backfill-overlaps`), every period already has a completed run (`nothing-to-run`), the pipeline is inactive (`pipeline-inactive`) or has no steps (`pipeline-not-backfillable`); 422 (`invalid-parameters`) when a value does not suit its parameter.

202.description: The backfill, made; its runs are queued gradually.

get.summary: A backfill, its progress and its periods.
get.description: The backfill's status (`running`, `paused`, `cancelled`, `completed` -- every period completed or skipped --, or `failed` -- at least one period failed), how many periods are in each state, why it waits when it does (`waitingReason`: the workspace is suspended, the pipeline is switched off), when it should end, and its first 100 periods with each one's run (follow a run as any run, `GET /runs/{runId}`). A failed period keeps its run's last message as `note`.

post.description: Nothing more is queued: its waiting periods are cancelled. The runs already started finish and are recorded on their periods. Refused (409 `backfill-closed`) when the backfill has ended already.

get.summary: Runs, newest first.
get.description: Every run of the workspace's pipelines, however it started (the API, an event, the console, a schedule), newest first. The filters combine. updatedAfter compares the run's latest time (its end, else its start, else its creation); createdAfter its creation. Times are RFC 3339 with an offset; a filter that is not one is 400.

get.summary: One run, with its status, times (UTC) and review status.

post.summary: Retry a failed run from the step that failed, or from the start.
post.description: Runs a failed run again as its next attempt (the same run id; `attempt` goes up by one). With no body, or `{"from": "failed_step"}`, it resumes from the first step of the latest attempt that did not complete: the steps before it are not run again -- their kept outputs are reused, and their work is not billed again -- and the step that failed and every step after it run, on the pipeline as it is now. `{"from": "start"}` runs every step again. A resume is refused (409, the problem's `type` says why) when the run is not failed (`run-not-failed`), another run of the pipeline is in flight (`run-in-flight`), the pipeline is inactive (`pipeline-inactive`) or its workspace paused (`workspace-paused`), the pipeline changed before the failed step (`pipeline-changed`: only the failed step and later steps may change; a step's name, retries, timeout and on-error may), a file a reused step read has changed since, judged by its sha256 (`input-changed`), a reused step's kept output has expired (`outputs-expired`: outputs are kept for the pipeline's retention, 24 hours unless set), or there is nothing to resume from (`not-resumable`: the run ran no steps, every step completed, or it has had 20 attempts). From the start, only the first four apply. Answered once the run is queued; follow it as any run, or by its `run.started` and `run.completed` or `run.failed` events, which carry the new `attempt` and `retry`.

202.description: The run, queued as its next attempt.

get.summary: The run's steps in order (its latest attempt).
get.description: The steps of the run's latest attempt, in order, with their status, rows in and out, and times. A run of a pipeline without steps is shown as its one step, key "legacy". A new kind of step appears here as it is, with its own task name: there is no endpoint per step kind.

get.summary: The run's manifest: the files it received and made, by file id, and its review.
get.description: The files the run's latest attempt made (role result, or report for a PDF) and, for a run started through the API, the files it was given (role input), each by its file id: GET /v1/files/{fileId} downloads it. A step that makes a PDF lists two files with the same step: the PDF (report), which prints the first rows of a big table, and the full data beside it as a CSV (result), unless the step turns that off. Never a bucket, a storage key or a connection. A made file is kept as long as the pipeline keeps its run's files (expiresAt); after that it is listed as expired and its download is 410.

get.summary: A completed run's answer: its final output's rows, masked, at most 100 rows and 16 KB -- or the run's report as PDF, HTML or Markdown.
get.description: The rows of the last step of the run's latest attempt that kept an output, as the pipeline's own data -- the answer a run-and-wait gives when the run ends in time. Every column the workspace's data policy marks sensitive (the Data Catalog's sensitive assets, and a person's details in a pipeline marked sensitive) is masked, and named in `masked`; at most 100 rows and 16 KB of JSON (`truncated` says when there were more). An output past the pipeline's retention, or a run that kept none, answers no rows and says why in `problem`. A run that has not completed is a 409 (`run-not-completed`); another workspace's run a 404. The format is the client's choice -- `format` (json, pdf, html, md), or the Accept header (application/json, application/pdf, text/html, text/markdown; a wildcard is json); json when neither says, and any other format is a 400 (`unsupported-format`) naming the allowed ones. pdf, html and md are the run's report (its Generate report step): its PDF -- the signed one once approved and signed --, its HTML, or Markdown made from that HTML (headings, tables and lists; pictures, signatures, charts and the QR code as links to the PDF), whose first line names it ("From signed report RPT-0093 version 1") -- Markdown is never signed: the PDF is the record. A run that made several reports (one per row) names one with `report` (else 409 `several-reports`, listing them in `reports`). Without a report, html and md are the result rows above as a table (masked the same way), and pdf is a 404 (`no-report`). A pipeline marked sensitive keeps its report from API clients in every format (403 `sensitive-files`), as its files; a report made without the format's source (a PDF-only report has no HTML, so no Markdown) is a 404 (`format-not-kept`); one whose files the workspace's retention removed is a 410 (`report-expired`). A document's answer says what it is made from in X-Result-Source (report or rows) and, for a report, X-Report, X-Report-Version and X-Report-Signed; it is never cached (Cache-Control: no-store) and comes as an attachment.

200.description: The run's result, in the format asked for.

get.summary: The run's items: each file, recording, document or row it processed one by one, with its status.
get.description: A pipeline that works item by item (a step per recording, per file, per document, per row of a per-row call, or one that splits a PDF into its pages) keeps one item per thing it processed: its status (running, done, failed), the step it failed at and why in words, how many of its sub-items (a document's pages) failed, and the files its steps made for it, by file id (GET /v1/files/{fileId} downloads one). In the run's order, cursor paging; parentId lists one item's sub-items. Any other run -- one that reads a table whole -- has no items: an empty list. An item retried in a later attempt shows its latest version (attempt). Never a bucket, a key in a bucket or a storage key.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: failed takes in an item with failed sub-items.

get.summary: One item of a run, with each of its steps.
get.description: The item by its id ("2"; a sub-item "3.12") -- or by its key, when the key has no '/'. As listRunItems lists it, with steps: each step's status for this item (done, failed, not_run, shared -- a combining step whose output belongs to many items, sharedBy saying how many -- or left_out, when a filter left the item out), its message, rows and files.

get.summary: The run's review: who must decide and what they decided.

post.summary: The customer's decision on a completed run (the CUSTOMER party).
post.description: The same rules as the console's review: the run is completed, its pipeline asks for a customer review (settings.review.required), the run's results are still pending, and the customer has not decided yet -- otherwise 409. A rejection says why (reason); rerun asks for the pipeline to run again as a new run, which only a run started through the API can be (it is started again with the same intake); a re-run that cannot start leaves the rejection standing and says why in rerun.message. Sending the same Idempotency-Key again returns the first answer.

post.summary: A signed, read-only link to the run's page (15 minutes) to embed in a portal.
post.description: A link to the console's page /embed/runs/{token}: the run's status and times, its steps, the files it made (each with a download) and its review, read-only, with no console navigation and no sign-in. Open it on its own or show it in an iframe: only the origins the API client's frame allow-list names may frame it (Developers › API Clients; the page answers Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors with them, 'none' when there are none), and it refuses everything once it has expired. Append `?theme=light` or `dark`, and `accent=<hex colour>` (e.g. 0b6bcb), to fit the portal. The link opens that one run only: no other run, no file it does not list, nothing of the API. A revoked client's links end at once. Nothing is stored and nothing is billed but this call, so no Idempotency-Key: each call answers a new link. Give each visitor a fresh link rather than a long-lived one.

expiresInSeconds.description: A shorter life than 15 minutes, for a link shown once.

get.summary: What a view link's page shows, through the link's own token.
get.description: No access token: the view link's token is the permission, for that one run, read-only, until it expires. The console's page reads this; a portal's server may too. Times are UTC. Each file the run made carries a download (a signed file link, GET /v1/files/{fileId}/content) that ends no later than the view. refreshSeconds says when a run that is still moving is worth reading again (null once it has settled). Not counted as an API call and not billed: a signed link is free, and only POST view-links is. 410 once expired (`/problems/link-expired`) or when the client that made it was revoked or has expired (`/problems/link-ended`); 404 for a token this API did not make.

200.description: The run as the page shows it.

get.summary: Who may frame a view link's page -- the console's server asks before serving it.
get.description: The origins the API client's frame allow-list names, also as the `Embed-Frame-Ancestors` header (a CSP source list, `'none'` when the list is empty), which the console's server sends as Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors with the page. An expired link still answers its origins (state `expired`), so the portal shows that it expired rather than a broken frame; its data is refused. 404, and frame-ancestors 'none', for a token this API did not make or a revoked client's.

200.description: Where the page may be framed.

post.summary: Upload a file for a run or a form; answers its file id.
post.description: Stored in the workspace's inbox (role input) and named by a ULID, the only id of a file a customer sees; nothing starts because of an upload. Its size is limited by the workspace (413), its kind is checked against its content (422). 409 when the workspace has no inbox yet, or for an Idempotency-Key reused with another file.

get.summary: Redirects to a signed link valid 5 minutes.
get.description: A file of the workspace's -- one it uploaded, or one a run made (the manifest's) -- answered with a 302 to its signed link on this API (/v1/files/{fileId}/content?token=...), valid 5 minutes. The link needs no token, so a portal may hand it to a browser; it opens that one file only, and never names a bucket or a storage key. The body says the same for a caller that does not follow redirects. A made file past its expiry is 410. A file a pipeline marked sensitive made (a saved file, a report's PDF) is the pipeline's real output, never masked: an API client is refused it with a 403 of type sensitive-files until a scope for it is offered -- its meta still describes it.

get.summary: The file's bytes, through the signed link GET /v1/files/{fileId} answered.
get.description: No access token: the link's signature is the permission, for this file only, until it expires (5 minutes). A link that has expired is 410 (ask GET /v1/files/{fileId} for a new one); a link that is not one this API made, or names another file, is 404. A file a pipeline marked sensitive made is 403 (sensitive-files), as GET /v1/files/{fileId}.

200.description: The bytes, as an attachment named by the file.

get.summary: A file's facts: name, size, sha256, role.
The active forms this client may fill in.
One form and its fields.

post.summary: Submit answers (file fields name file ids); starts the form's pipeline or workflow when it has one.

get.summary: One submission and the run it started.

200.description: The submission and the run it started.

post.summary: An event from the organisation's systems; the workspace's event routes start what it names.
post.description: The type is the organisation's own; the workspace's event routes (set in the console) say which pipeline or workflow it starts, and may name a data contract the data must meet (422 with each field's path under "data", nothing started). A type no route takes is 422 at "type". Each route's pipeline gets a run with the data as its record; each workflow route a request whose subject is the event. What could not start is in notStarted, with why (a run of that pipeline still in flight, say).

type.description: The organisation's own event type, e.g. "order.received".

notStarted.description: What a route names that did not start, and why.

target.description: The pipeline's id or the workflow's key.

get.summary: The catalogue of event types the platform sends (each with its JSON Schema).
get.description: A registry, not a fixed list: a new event type appears here, and becomes subscribable, when the platform adds it. Each entry's schema is the JSON Schema of the event's data, self-contained.

get.summary: The webhook subscriptions.

post.summary: Subscribe a URL to event types; the signing secret is shown once.
post.description: The URL must be https and every address its host resolves to public: a private, loopback, link-local or metadata address is refused here (422 at url), and again at every delivery. A workspace has at most 20 webhooks (409). Only events that happen after the webhook is made are sent to it. In a workspace our team manages, webhooks are set up by our team: making, changing, removing and rotating are 403 there.

secret.description: Shown once (and in a replay of this request under its Idempotency-Key).

get.summary: One subscription.

patch.summary: Change the URL, the event types, or pause it.
patch.description: active false pauses the webhook: nothing more is sent to it, and what was still waiting is marked failed. active true resumes it (and clears a pause the platform made after repeated failures); only events after that are sent.

delete.summary: Remove a subscription; nothing more is sent to it.

post.summary: A new secret; the old one is accepted alongside it for 24 hours.

get.summary: A subscription's delivery attempts, newest first.

post.description: A new delivery of the same event (the same Webhook-Id), sent within seconds and retried like any other; it names the delivery it repeats. The webhook must be active (409 when paused), and the event still kept.

A POST of the event to the subscription's URL. Verify `Webhook-Signature: t=<unix seconds>, v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>" keyed by the subscription's secret>` -- for 24 hours after a rotation there is one v1 per secret, the new one first; accept when any matches -- refuse a t more than 5 minutes from your clock, and answer 2xx within 10 seconds. Anything else (another status, no answer, a redirect) is a failed attempt, retried after 10 s, 30 s, 90 s ... at most an hour apart, for 24 hours; then the delivery is failed. A webhook that has failed for 3 days with no success is paused, and its maker told. Delivery is at least once: deduplicate on Webhook-Id. One webhook's first attempts go out in the order the events happened; a retry does not hold later events back, so order by createdAt.

parameters.name: Webhook-Id
parameters.description: The event id; the same on every retry and redelivery.

parameters.name: Webhook-Delivery
parameters.description: This delivery's id, as the delivery log shows it.

scopes.runs:read: Read runs, steps, outputs and reviews; create view links.
scopes.webhooks:manage: Manage webhook subscriptions and read the event catalogue.

ViewToken.name: token
ViewToken.description: The token of a view link's URL.

ResultFormat.name: format
ResultFormat.description: json (the default), pdf, html or md. Wins over Accept. Anything else is a 400 (unsupported-format).

ResultReport.name: report
ResultReport.description: pdf, html and md of a run that made several reports: which one, by its number (RPT-0093).

ResultAccept.name: Accept
ResultAccept.description: Without format: application/json, application/pdf, text/html or text/markdown (by q, then order; */* is json). An Accept naming none of them is a 400 (unsupported-format). For POST /pipelines/{pipelineId}/runs only with wait.

Forbidden.description: A scope is missing or the address is not allowed.

Conflict.description: An Idempotency-Key reused with a different body, or the wrong state.

Gone.description: No longer there: a file past its expiry, or a link that has expired.

Unprocessable.description: The input contract refused it; errors name each field.

Unavailable.description: Temporarily unavailable; try again after Retry-After.

TooManyRequests.description:
Past a limit. `/problems/rate-limited`: the client's rate limit, or its workspace's limit over all its clients;
try again after Retry-After seconds (when a token is back). `/problems/quota-exceeded`: the workspace has used its
monthly quota of calls; Retry-After is the seconds until the month (the bill's, in the workspace's billing time zone)
ends. Nothing was done and nothing billed.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

X-Result-Source.description: A document's source: report (the run's report) or rows (its result rows; no report).

X-Report.description: The report a document is made from (RPT-0093); absent for rows.

X-Report-Signed.description: Whether that version is approved and signed (its PDF is the signed one). Markdown is never signed itself.

RateLimit-Limit.description: The size of the bucket that allows fewer calls now (the client's burst, or its workspace's): on every answer to a call that was counted.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Calls you may make right now.

RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until that bucket is full again (or, refused, until one call is allowed).

RateLimit-Policy.description: That bucket's rate: calls a minute, the window, its burst and whose it is, e.g. 600;w=60;burst=100;scope=client.

Quota-Limit.description: The workspace's monthly quota of calls, when it has one.

Quota-Remaining.description: Calls left in the quota this month (the bill's month, in the workspace's billing time zone).

Quota-Reset.description: Seconds until the month (the bill's, in the workspace's billing time zone) ends and the quota starts again.

Quota-Warning.description: From 80% of the quota used, e.g. "85% of this month's 10000 API calls are used."

bad-request.title: Bad Request
bad-request.description: The request cannot be read: not JSON, a filter that is not RFC 3339 with an offset, a missing or malformed Idempotency-Key.

unauthorized.title: Unauthorized
unauthorized.description: No valid access token: none, expired (15 minutes), or revoked by a secret rotation, a change of scopes or a revoked client. Ask for a new token. The token endpoint also answers OAuth's own `error` (invalid_client, invalid_scope, ...).

forbidden.title: Forbidden
forbidden.description: The caller's address is not on the client's allowlist.

insufficient-scope.title: Forbidden
insufficient-scope.description: The token does not carry the scope the operation needs. Give the client the scope, then ask for a new token.

managed-workspace.title: Forbidden
managed-workspace.description: In a workspace our team manages, making, changing, removing and rotating webhooks is our team's.

not-found.title: Not Found
not-found.description: Not there, or not yours: the same answer for another workspace's id. An undeclared /v1 path is one too.

conflict.title: Conflict
conflict.description: The resource's state refuses it, e.g. a redelivery while the webhook is paused or a workspace's 21st webhook.

idempotency-conflict.title: Conflict
idempotency-conflict.description: This Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request (within 24 hours). Use a new key for new work.

idempotency-in-progress.title: Conflict
idempotency-in-progress.description: A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being handled. Try again in a moment with the same key.

run-in-flight.title: Conflict
run-in-flight.description: A run of this pipeline is still in flight; one runs at a time. Start (or retry) the next once it has finished.

workspace-paused.title: Conflict
workspace-paused.description: The workspace is suspended or inactive, so its runs are paused.

run-not-completed.title: Conflict
run-not-completed.description: The run has not completed (queued, running, failed, skipped or interrupted), so it has no result.

unsupported-format.title: Bad Request
unsupported-format.description: format (or Accept) names no format the result is given in: json, pdf, html or md (application/json, application/pdf, text/html, text/markdown).

no-report.title: Not Found
no-report.description: The run made no report, so it has no PDF; json, html and md give its result rows. Add a Generate report step for a PDF.

no-such-report.title: Not Found
no-such-report.description: report names a report the run did not make; the problem names the ones it did.

format-not-kept.title: Not Found
format-not-kept.description: The run's report was made without this format's source: a PDF-only report has no HTML, so no Markdown either. Ask for a format it has, or add the format to the Generate report step.

several-reports.title: Conflict
several-reports.description: The run made several reports (one per row); name one with report=RPT-… (`reports` lists them), or read each item's files.

report-expired.title: Gone
report-expired.description: The report's files were removed by the workspace's retention policy; its record stays. Run the pipeline again for a new report.

sensitive-files.title: Forbidden
sensitive-files.description: The pipeline is marked sensitive: its files, and its report in every format (pdf, html, md), are downloaded in the console, not through the API. json stays masked.

run-not-failed.title: Conflict
run-not-failed.description: Only a failed run is retried; this one is queued, running, completed, skipped or interrupted.

pipeline-changed.title: Conflict
pipeline-changed.description: The pipeline changed before the step that failed (its source, or a step's key, task, input or settings), so the kept outputs no longer match it. Retry with from start.

input-changed.title: Conflict
input-changed.description: A file a step before the failed one read has changed since (its sha256), or is gone; a resume would mix old and new data. Retry with from start.

outputs-expired.title: Conflict
outputs-expired.description: A kept output of a step before the failed one has expired (outputs are kept for the pipeline's retention, 24 hours unless set). Retry with from start.

not-resumable.title: Conflict
not-resumable.description: There is no step to resume from (the run ran no steps, or every step completed), its inputs cannot be checked, or it has had 20 attempts. Retry with from start, or start a new run.

too-many-backfills.title: Conflict
too-many-backfills.description: The workspace already has 3 open (running or paused) backfills. Wait for one to finish, or cancel one.

backfill-overlaps.title: Conflict
backfill-overlaps.description: A day of the range is already in another open backfill of the pipeline. Pick a range after it, or cancel that backfill.

nothing-to-run.title: Conflict
nothing-to-run.description: Every period of the range already has a completed run. Ask with rerunCompleted true to run them again.

pipeline-not-backfillable.title: Conflict
pipeline-not-backfillable.description: The pipeline has no steps, so it cannot be backfilled.

backfill-closed.title: Conflict
backfill-closed.description: The backfill has ended already (completed, failed or cancelled).

invalid-parameters.title: Unprocessable Content
invalid-parameters.description: A parameter value does not suit its parameter (its type, its choices), a required one has no value, or the pipeline has no parameter of that name.

workspace-not-ready.title: Conflict
workspace-not-ready.description: The workspace has no inbox for API uploads yet; an administrator chooses one under Documents › Intake › File drop.

review-not-open.title: Conflict
review-not-open.description: The run's review cannot take this decision: not completed, no customer review asked for, or already decided.

file-expired.title: Gone
file-expired.description: The file is past its expiry: still listed (expired true), no longer downloadable. Run the pipeline again for a new one.

link-expired.title: Gone
link-expired.description: A signed link (a file link, 5 minutes; a view link, 15 minutes) has expired. Ask for a new one.

link-ended.title: Gone
link-ended.description: The API client that made the view link was revoked or has expired, so its links ended at once.

too-large.title: Content Too Large
too-large.description: An upload over 100 MB, or a JSON body over 1 MB.

unsupported-media-type.title: Unsupported Media Type
unsupported-media-type.description: The body is not the content type the operation takes (JSON, multipart/form-data, or a form for the token).

validation.title: Unprocessable Content
validation.description: The input contract (or the request's own rules) refused it; `errors[]` names each field by its path (`record.amount`) and why, never echoing a value.

rate-limited.title: Too Many Requests
rate-limited.description: Past the client's rate limit, or its workspace's over all its clients. Wait Retry-After seconds.

quota-exceeded.title: Too Many Requests
quota-exceeded.description: The workspace has used its monthly quota of calls. Retry-After is the seconds until the month (the bill's, in the workspace's billing time zone) ends.

bad-gateway.title: Bad Gateway
bad-gateway.description: The service behind the call could not be reached, or dropped the connection before answering. Try again in a moment, with the same Idempotency-Key for a write.

unavailable.title: Service Unavailable
unavailable.description: Something the answer needs cannot be reached just now (the limits store, an input contract). Try again after Retry-After.

timeout.title: Gateway Timeout
timeout.description: The service behind the call did not answer in time: 30 seconds, 120 for uploading a file (POST /files) and a file's content. A write may still have been made: repeat it with the same Idempotency-Key, which answers what was done or does it once. Once a download has started it is never cut while it keeps flowing; one silent for 30 seconds is ended.

ReviewStatus.description: not_applicable: the pipeline asks for a review, but the run ended without results (failed, skipped, interrupted or missed) -- nothing waits for a reviewer.

inputContract.description: The JSON Schema a started run's record must meet (the data contract the pipeline names); null when it names none.

acceptsFiles.description: Whether a run may name files (a step pipeline reads them from its intake).

parameters.description: Its run parameters (a backfill's `parameters` gives their values; a run takes each one's default otherwise).

reference.description: The organisation's own id for this work, echoed back.

parameters.description: The run's parameter values by name, as the pipeline declares them (GET /pipelines/{id}: parameters).

step.description: The key of the step whose output this is.

rowCount.description: How many rows the output has; rows holds at most 100 of them.

truncated.description: More rows (or more than 16 KB) than given.

masked.description: The columns masked by the workspace's data policy.

problem.description: Why there are no rows: past its retention, or the run kept no output.

result.description: A completed run's result; null for a run that failed, was skipped or interrupted.

attempt.description: Which attempt the run is on, from 1. A retry (POST /runs/{runId}/retry, or the console's) is the next attempt of the same run.

retry.description: How the run's current attempt came about when someone retried it; null for a first attempt or one the pipeline's own retry policy made.

from.description: failed_step: resumed from the step that failed; start: every step ran again.

fromStep.description: The key of the step it resumed from; null from the start.

reusedSteps.description: How many steps before it were not run again (their kept outputs reused).

from.description: The first day, in the workspace's billing time zone.

to.description: The last day (included); not after today there.

step.description: One run per day, hour or week.

concurrency.description: Runs in flight at once (the platform may allow fewer).

rerunCompleted.description: Run again the periods that already have a completed run.

parameters.description: The pipeline's parameters by name (GET /pipelines/{pipelineId} lists them); one not given takes its default.

timeZone.description: The billing time zone its periods are counted in.

parameters.description: The values given (normalised); the rest are the defaults.

waitingReason.description: Why nothing is queued just now, while it is running.

periods.description: Its first 100 periods, oldest first (GET only).

task.description: The step's task, e.g. read_file, validate, save_file, generate_report; legacy for a run without steps.

reusedFromAttempt.description: A step a retry did not run again: the attempt whose output it reused (it has no times of its own). Null for a step that ran.

attempt.description: The attempt whose files are listed: the run's latest.

summary.description: Over the run's items (not sub-items): failed counts an item with failed sub-items.

id.description: The item's id in the run: "2", a sub-item "3.12". The same in every attempt.

key.description: What names the item: the file's path in the run's own folder, a document id, a row's key.

failedStep.description: The key of the step it failed at.

attempt.description: The run attempt this version of the item is from: a retried item's latest.

step.description: The step that made it (null for an input).

rows.description: Rows it holds, for a data file.

expired.description: Past expiresAt: listed, no longer downloadable (410).

id.description: A ULID; the only id of a file a customer sees.

sha256.description: Hex; null for a file a run made before files carried one.

sensitive.description: Present (true) on a file a pipeline marked sensitive made: listed here, refused by GET /v1/files/{fileId} and its link (403 sensitive-files).

downloadable.description: Present (false) beside sensitive: an API client cannot download it yet.

url.description: The signed link, as Location says it.
The console's page /embed/runs/{token}; add ?theme= and &accent= to fit.

RunView.description: A Run (review as the full Review), with its pipeline's name, steps, made files with downloads, and the view's own expiry.

files.description: The files the run's latest attempt made (role result or report).

download.description: A signed file link (null once the file has expired), ending no later than the view.

refreshSeconds.description: Read again after this many seconds while the run is still moving.

rerunRunId.description: The run that ran the pipeline again after a rejection.

rerun.description: Only in the answer to a rejection with rerun.
On a rejection, run the pipeline again.

help.description: A short hint shown under the field. Display text only, never markup; absent when it has none.

placeholder.description: Example text shown inside the field's empty control (text, longText, number, date, email, choice and lookup fields only). One line of display text, never markup and never a substitute for `label`; absent when it has none.

options.description: A choice's options, or a checkboxes field's (each one the person may tick).

section.description: The title of the group the field belongs to: consecutive fields with the same section are shown together under its heading. One line of display text; absent when the field is not grouped.

minSelected.description: checkboxes: the fewest options to tick once any is ticked; absent when there is no least.

maxSelected.description: checkboxes: the most options that may be ticked; absent when there is no most.

items.description: type is one of text, longText, number, date, choice, checkboxes, yesNo, email, table, file, signature or lookup. A checkboxes answer is the list of the options ticked, in the options' order (in a form's CSV export they are joined with "; ").

runId.description: The run it started, if the form starts one.

schema.description: JSON Schema of the event's data.

pausedReason.description: Why it is paused: by its owner, or by the platform after 3 days of failures.

failingSince.description: The first failed attempt since the last success.

previousSecretValidUntil.description: While the previous secret still signs beside the new one.

ResultFormats.description: The formats run.completed carries the run's result in, as data.results (WebhookRunResults): json, pdf, html, md -- each once, in the order given; [] (the default) sends the Run alone, as before. An unknown one is a 422 at resultFormats[i]. Asked at each attempt, so a retry or a redelivery carries the result as it stands then.

WebhookRunResults.description: run.completed's data.results, for a webhook with resultFormats -- the same answers as GET /runs/{runId}/result in each format: json the RunResult (masked); md and html the text, pdf base64, each from the run's report (the signed PDF once signed; Markdown made from its HTML, never signed) or, with no report, html and md from the result rows. A format the run cannot be given in -- a sensitive pipeline's report (403), no report for a PDF (404), several reports (409), or past the 5 MB of documents a delivery carries (413, read it with the API) -- is in problems instead, by format.

report.description: The report it is made from; null for the result rows.

attempt.description: Attempts made so far (0 while the first is pending).

responseStatus.description: The last answer's status; null when none came.

error.description: Why the last attempt failed, never the answer's body.

redeliveryOf.description: The delivery this one sends again.
